content.intro: In this lesson, you will study introduction to Data in AI within Data Fundamentals and Preparation. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Data records observations or representations of a phenomenon. Choose formats and measurements that fit the task, document their meaning, and verify that the dataset represents the population and conditions where the system will be used.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics covered in this lesson

items.title: What data represents
items.text: What data represents is one of the concepts used to reason about introduction to data in ai. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data
items.text: Structured data follows a defined schema; semi-structured formats carry organization without one rigid table schema; unstructured data includes forms such as free text, images, and audio. The storage format influences preprocessing and evaluation.

items.title: Numerical and categorical data
items.text: Numerical and categorical data is one of the concepts used to reason about introduction to data in ai. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Text, images, audio, video, and sensor data
items.text: Text, images, audio, video, and sensor data is one of the concepts used to reason about introduction to data in ai. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Data quality and data suitability
items.text: Data quality includes accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and fitness for the intended task. Clean-looking records can still fail to represent the target population or real deployment conditions.

clean = []

    seen.add(row["id"])
    clean.append(row)

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. If the example runs as expected, do not infer that it proves a trained model works; this snippet is a deterministic teaching aid. Keep sensitive data out of tests.

content_blocks.title: Check before you trust a result
content_blocks.text: This is a small, deterministic teaching example—not a trained AI model or evidence of production performance. Run it with a local Python 3 interpreter; do not paste secrets or private data into experiments.
